data.name: Alroy
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name Alaric, meaning 'ruler of all the people'. In Christian legend, Alaric was a 5th-century Gothic king who converted to Christianity and is said to have led his people to Rome in a peaceful conquest. The name Alroy can be seen as a symbol of leadership and protection in a Christian context.

in_hebrew.name: אלרוי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אלרוי הוא שם שמשמעותו 'אל שומעני' או 'אל רואה אותי', מורכב מ'אל' - האל, ו'רוי' - רואה או שומע. השם קשור לאלוהים כמי ששומע ורואה את עמו.

in_greek.name: Αλρόυ
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι ο Θεός που με βλέπει
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Αλρόυ προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'אל' (Θεός) και 'רוי' (με βλέπει ή με ακούει). Σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι ο Θεός που με βλέπει' ή 'Ο Θεός που ακούει', υπογραμμίζοντας την παντογνωσία και την παρουσία του Θεού στη ζωή των ανθρώπων.

in_latin.name: Alroy
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Alroy derivatur ex verbis hebraicis 'אל' (Deus) et 'רוי' (videt vel audit). Significat 'Deus est qui me videt' vel 'Deus qui audit', referens ad omniscientiam et providentiam Dei in vita hominum.

in_english.name: Alroy
in_english.meaning: God is the one who sees or hears me
in_english.long_meaning: The name Alroy originates from Hebrew roots 'אל' (El, meaning God) and 'רוי' (roi, meaning sees or hears). It translates to 'God is the one who sees me' or 'God who hears me', signifying God's omnipresence, omniscience, and personal relationship with His people. Historically, the name reflects the biblical concept of God as a personal and caring deity.

biblical_reference.note: In Genesis 16:13, Hagar names God 'El-Roi', meaning 'The God who sees me', after encountering Him in the wilderness.
